method_card.title: Area & Perimeter Formulas
steps: Pick the shape and its formula.
Put in the given lengths, using the perpendicular height for triangles and parallelograms.
Work it out and add the unit: cm² for area, cm for length.
For a compound shape, split into parts and add or subtract the areas.
method_card.content: Rectangle area is length times width; its perimeter is twice the sum of length and width. A triangle is half of base times height. A parallelogram is base times perpendicular height. A trapezium is half of the two parallel sides added, times the height. A circle has area \(\pi r^2\) and circumference \(2\pi r\). A sector or arc takes the angle over 360 as its fraction of the whole circle.
method_card.example: Trapezium, parallel sides 8 cm and 12 cm, height 5 cm: area = \(\tfrac{1}{2}(8 + 12) \times 5 = 50\) cm².

bronze.display: Area of a rectangle 7 cm by 5 cm.Diagram not drawn accurately

misconceptions.message: That is the perimeter. Area = length × width = 7 × 5 = 35 cm².
Multiply, do not add: 7 × 5 = 35 cm².

guided_steps.say: Area of a rectangle = length × width.
Now multiply length by width.

guided_steps.hint: Divide the area by the width.
guided_steps.done: That gives the length 7 cm back, so 35 cm² is right.

bronze.display: Perimeter of a rectangle 9 cm by 4 cm.Diagram not drawn accurately
bronze.hint: Add length and width, then double.

misconceptions.message: That is the area. Perimeter = 2(9 + 4) = 26 cm.
Add length + width then double: 2(9 + 4) = 26.

guided_steps.say: Perimeter = the distance all the way round = 2 × (length + width).
Double it: there are two of each side.

guided_steps.done: That is 9 + 4 again, so 26 cm is right.

bronze.display: Area of a triangle: base 12 cm, height 8 cm.Diagram not drawn accurately
bronze.hint: Multiply base by height, then halve.

misconceptions.message: Triangle area = ½ × base × height. Do not forget the ½: 96 ÷ 2 = 48.
Multiply base by height, then halve. Do not add.

guided_steps.say: Triangle area = ½ × base × height.
A triangle is half of its surrounding rectangle.

guided_steps.done: That is 12 × 8, the full rectangle, so 48 cm² is right.

bronze.display: Area of a parallelogram: base 10 cm, perpendicular height 6 cm.Diagram not drawn accurately
bronze.hint: Base times perpendicular height, no halving.

misconceptions.message: A parallelogram is not halved: area = base × height = 60 cm².
Multiply base and height, do not add: 10 × 6 = 60.

guided_steps.say: Parallelogram area = base × perpendicular height. No halving.

guided_steps.hint: The straight-up height, not a slanted side.

guided_steps.say: Multiply base by height, and stop there.

guided_steps.done: That gives the height 6 cm back, so 60 cm² is right.

bronze.display: A square has perimeter 36 cm. What is its area?Diagram not drawn accurately
bronze.hint: Find one side (perimeter ÷ 4) first, then square it.

misconceptions.message: 9 cm is the side length. Area = 9 × 9 = 81 cm².
36 cm is the perimeter, not the area. Find the side, then square it.

guided_steps.say: A square has four equal sides. Find one side first, then square it.

guided_steps.hint: Perimeter shared into four equal sides.

guided_steps.say: Area of a square = side × side.

guided_steps.done: That rebuilds the 36 cm perimeter, so 81 cm² is right.

bronze.display: Area of a triangle: base 14 cm, height 6 cm.Diagram not drawn accurately
bronze.hint: Multiply base by height, then halve.

misconceptions.message: ½ × 14 × 6 = 42. Remember the ½.
Area = ½ × base × height, not base + height.

guided_steps.say: Triangle area = ½ × base × height.
Then take half.

guided_steps.done: That is 14 × 6, so 42 cm² is right.

bronze.display: A rectangle has area 48 cm² and length 8 cm. What is the width?Diagram not drawn accurately
bronze.hint: Divide the area by the length.

misconceptions.message: Width = area ÷ length = 48 ÷ 8 = 6 cm, not 48 × 8.
Divide the area by the length to find the width.

guided_steps.say: Area = length × width, so width = area ÷ length.

guided_steps.hint: Given in the question, in cm².

guided_steps.say: Divide the area by the length.

guided_steps.done: That rebuilds the 48 cm² area, so the width is 6 cm.

bronze.display: Perimeter of an equilateral triangle with side 9 cm.Diagram not drawn accurately
bronze.hint: Three equal sides: multiply the side by 3.

misconceptions.message: An equilateral triangle has 3 sides, so 3 × 9 = 27, not 2 × 9.
Perimeter adds the sides: 3 × 9 = 27. That is not 9².

guided_steps.say: An equilateral triangle has three equal sides. Perimeter = 3 × side.

guided_steps.hint: Equilateral means all three the same.

guided_steps.say: Add the three equal 9 cm sides.

guided_steps.done: That gives one 9 cm side back, so 27 cm is right.

silver.display: Circumference of a circle with radius 7 cm. (Use π = 3.14)Diagram not drawn accurately

misconceptions.message: That is the area (πr²). Circumference = 2πr = 2 × 3.14 × 7 = 43.96 cm.
7 is the radius. Use C = 2πr = 43.96 cm, not πr.

guided_steps.say: Circumference = 2 × π × r. Here r = 7 and π = 3.14.

guided_steps.hint: Double the radius to get the diameter.

guided_steps.say: Multiply by π.

guided_steps.done: That is 2 × 7, so 43.96 cm is right.

silver.display: Area of a circle with diameter 10 cm. Give your answer to 1 d.p.Diagram not drawn accurately
silver.hint: Halve the diameter, then use π r².

misconceptions.message: Radius = 5 cm. Area = π × 5² = 78.5 cm², not π × 10².
Area = πr², not 2πr. 2π × 5 = 31.4 is a length.

guided_steps.say: Area = π × r². The diameter is 10, so halve it for the radius.
Multiply by π and round.

guided_steps.done: That is 5², so 78.5 cm² is right.

silver.display: Area of a trapezium: parallel sides 6 cm and 10 cm, height 4 cm.Diagram not drawn accurately
silver.hint: Add the parallel sides, times height, then halve.

misconceptions.message: Area = ½(a + b)h = ½ × 16 × 4 = 32 cm². Remember the ½.
Add BOTH parallel sides: 6 + 10 = 16, not just one side.

guided_steps.say: Trapezium area = ½ × (a + b) × h, where a and b are the parallel sides.
Then take half.

guided_steps.hint: Undo the half and the height.
guided_steps.done: That is 6 + 10, so 32 cm² is right.

silver.display: Arc length of a sector: radius 10 cm, angle 72°. (1 d.p.)Diagram not drawn accurately
silver.hint: Take the angle over 360 as a fraction of 2 π r.

misconceptions.message: Multiply by the fraction 72/360 = 0.2: arc = 0.2 × 2π × 10 = 12.6 cm.
The fraction is 72/360 = 0.2, not 360/72 = 5.

guided_steps.say: Arc length = (angle ÷ 360) × 2 × π × r. Find the full circumference first.
Take that fraction of the circumference.

guided_steps.done: 0.2 is one fifth, so 12.6 cm is right.

silver.display: Area of a sector: radius 6 cm, angle 120°. (1 d.p.)Diagram not drawn accurately
silver.hint: Take the angle over 360 as a fraction of π r².

misconceptions.message: Multiply by the fraction 120/360 = 1/3: area = π × 36 ÷ 3 = 37.7 cm².
Area uses πr², not 2πr. (1/3) × 2π × 6 = 12.6 is a length.

guided_steps.say: Sector area = (angle ÷ 360) × π × r². Full circle area first.

guided_steps.hint: A third of the full area.
guided_steps.say: 120° is a third of 360°.

guided_steps.done: That rebuilds the full circle area, so 37.7 cm² is right.

silver.display: A semicircle has diameter 14 cm. Find its area. (1 d.p.)Diagram not drawn accurately
silver.hint: Halve the diameter, find π r², then halve for a semicircle.

misconceptions.message: A semicircle is HALF a circle: ½ × π × 7² = 77.0 cm².
Use radius 7 cm, not diameter 14 cm, in πr².

guided_steps.say: A semicircle is half a circle. Area = ½ × π × r². Diameter 14, so radius 7.

guided_steps.hint: Share the circle area in two.
guided_steps.say: A semicircle is half the circle.

guided_steps.hint: How many halves in the whole?
guided_steps.done: The full circle is twice the semicircle, so 77.0 cm² is right.

silver.display: A semicircle has radius 5 cm. Find its perimeter (the curved part plus the diameter). (1 d.p.)Diagram not drawn accurately
silver.hint: Curved part is π r; add the straight diameter 2r.

misconceptions.message: Add the straight diameter too: perimeter = π × 5 + 2 × 5 = 25.7 cm.
The curved part is HALF the circumference (πr), not the full 2πr.

guided_steps.say: The perimeter of a semicircle = the curved part + the straight diameter = π r + 2r.

guided_steps.pre: Curved part (half the circumference): π × 5, to 1 d.p. =

guided_steps.say: Curved plus straight.

guided_steps.done: That leaves the curved part π × 5, so 25.7 cm is right.

gold.display: A compound shape: rectangle 10 cm × 6 cm with a quarter-circle (radius 6 cm) removed. Find the area. (1 d.p.)Diagram not drawn accurately
gold.hint: Rectangle area minus the quarter-circle removed.

misconceptions.message: The quarter-circle is REMOVED, so subtract: 60 − 28.27 = 31.7 cm².
It is a quarter-circle, not a semicircle. Subtract ¼π(6²) = 28.27, not ½π(6²).

guided_steps.say: Find the rectangle, then subtract the quarter-circle that has been removed.
Take the removed piece away and round.

guided_steps.done: That rebuilds the rectangle, so 31.7 cm² is right.

gold.display: A circle has area 154 cm². Find its radius. (1 d.p.)Diagram not drawn accurately
gold.hint: Divide the area by π, then square-root.

misconceptions.message: 49.0 is r². Take the square root: r = √49 = 7.0 cm.
Use A = πr², so r = √(A/π) = 7.0. Do not use A = 2πr.

guided_steps.say: Area = π r². Work backwards: divide by π, then square-root.

guided_steps.pre: Divide the area by π: 154 ÷ π, to 1 d.p. =

guided_steps.say: Undo the squaring.

guided_steps.done: That rebuilds the 154 cm² area, so r = 7.0 cm.

gold.display: A sector has area 24π cm² and radius 12 cm. Find the angle.Diagram not drawn accurately
gold.hint: The π cancels; solve 24 = (θ/360) × 144 for θ.

misconceptions.message: Square the radius: use r² = 144, not r = 12. Then θ = 60°.
24π is an AREA, so use πr² (144π), not the arc formula 2πr.

guided_steps.say: Sector area = (θ ÷ 360) × π r². Set it equal to 24π and the π cancels.
Cancel π, then rearrange for θ.

guided_steps.done: That is the 24 (before the π), so 60° is right.

gold.display: A running track is two straights (100 m each) and two semicircles (diameter 60 m). Find the total length. (nearest m)Diagram not drawn accurately
gold.hint: Two straights plus one full circle (πd) for the two ends.

misconceptions.message: Add the curved ends too: the two semicircles make a full circle, πd = 188.5 m.
60 m is the DIAMETER, so C = π × 60 = 188.5 m, not 2π × 60.

guided_steps.say: The two straights are one length; the two semicircular ends make one full circle. Add them.

guided_steps.pre: The two ends make one circle, diameter 60. Circumference = π × 60, to 1 d.p. =

guided_steps.say: Add the straights and the curved ends.

guided_steps.pre: The fuller value is 388.49, just under 388.5, so to the nearest metre it is
guided_steps.say: Round to the nearest metre.

guided_steps.done: That is the curved circle length π × 60 ≈ 188.5, so 388 m is right.

gold.display: An annulus has outer radius 10 cm and inner radius 6 cm. Find its area. (1 d.p.)Diagram not drawn accurately
gold.hint: Outer circle area minus inner circle area.

misconceptions.message: Subtract AREAS, not radii: π(10²) − π(6²) = 64π = 201.1 cm².
An annulus is a ring: subtract the inner circle from the outer circle.

guided_steps.say: An annulus is a ring: outer circle area minus inner circle area.
Take the hole out of the disc.

guided_steps.done: That rebuilds the outer circle, so 201.1 cm² is right.

problem_bank.bronze_description: Area and perimeter of rectangles, triangles, parallelograms and squares
problem_bank.gold_description: Compound shapes, reverse problems, sectors and the annulus

worked_examples.question: Find the area of a triangle with base 10 cm and height 6 cm.
Find the area of a sector with radius 8 cm and angle 90°.
A compound shape is a rectangle 12 cm by 8 cm with a semicircle of diameter 8 cm removed. Find the shaded area.

bronze.title: Bronze: rectangles, triangles and parallelograms
steps: Triangle: area = ½ × base × height, using the perpendicular height.
Parallelogram: area = base × perpendicular height, no halving. A square's side is its perimeter ÷ 4.

example.question: Find the area of a triangle with base 10 cm and height 6 cm.

silver.title: Silver: circles, sectors and trapeziums
steps: Circle: area = \(\pi r^2\); circumference = \(2\pi r\). Halve a diameter to get the radius first.
Sector: take the fraction (angle ÷ 360) of the whole circle: of the area for a sector area, of \(2\pi r\) for an arc.
Trapezium: area = ½ × (a + b) × h, adding the two parallel sides.

example.question: Find the area of a sector with radius 8 cm and angle 90°.

gold.title: Gold: compound shapes and reverse problems
steps: Split a compound shape into simple parts, then add areas that join or subtract a piece that is removed.
For a reverse problem, run the formula backwards: to find a radius from an area, divide by \(\pi\) then square-root.
An annulus (a ring) is the outer circle area minus the inner circle area.

example.question: A rectangle 12 cm by 8 cm has a semicircle of diameter 8 cm removed. Find the area.

steps.pre: How many tiles cover the whole floor?
steps.hint: 5 tiles in each row, and there are 3 rows: 5 × 3.

steps.say: You worked out 5 × 3 = 15. Counting how many unit squares fill a shape IS finding its area. So area of a rectangle = length × width.

steps.pre: Now walk right around the very edge, one tile-length at a time. How many tile-lengths is the whole loop?

steps.say: That loop is the perimeter: the distance all the way round, \(2 \times (5 + 3) = 16\). Area fills the inside; perimeter measures the border. Every problem ahead uses one or the other.

bronze.display: Diagram not drawn accurately

steps.say: A rectangle is 8 cm by 5 cm. Find its area, then its perimeter.
Now the perimeter: add all four sides, which is 2 × (length + width).

steps.hint: Divide the area by the length.
steps.done: That gives the width 5 cm back, so area 40 cm² and perimeter 26 cm are right.

steps.say: A sector has radius 9 cm and angle 120°. Find its area, to 1 d.p.
120° out of 360° is one third of the circle.

steps.hint: Share the full area into three.

steps.done: That rebuilds the full circle area, so 84.8 cm² is right.

steps.say: A rectangle 10 cm by 4 cm has a semicircle of diameter 4 cm added on one end. Find the total area, to 1 d.p.
The semicircle has diameter 4, so radius 2.
